questions.prompt: What is a community in ecology?
options: All the different species living together in an area
Only one species in an area
questions.explanation: A community is all the populations of all different species living together in one area.
questions.misconception: One species is a population, not a community - a community includes many species together.

questions.prompt: Which is an interaction between community members?
questions.explanation: Community members interact by eating, competing, and helping each other.
questions.misconception: Rocks, rain, and sun are nonliving parts of the ecosystem, not community interactions.

questions.prompt: Are nonliving things like rocks and water part of a community?
options: No - those are part of the ecosystem, not the community
questions.explanation: A community is only the living things. Nonliving surroundings like rocks, water, and soil are part of the larger ecosystem.
questions.misconception: Community = living only; ecosystem = living + nonliving. That distinction is the key.

questions.prompt: What is a community made of?
questions.explanation: A community is built from many populations - all the different species present in the area.
questions.misconception: Communities include plants, animals, fungi, and microbes - all species, not just one group.
